overview: Treyarnon is a smallish sandy beach west of St Merryn near Padstow, right next to Constantine Bay, with a car park, toilets, a beach shop, a café and a youth hostel. It’s a favourite for bodyboarding, has lifeguards in summer and, nicely for dog owners, allows dogs all year.

At low tide there’s a partly man-made rock pool on the rocks that works like a natural swimming pool for older children, and at the end of the headland is Trethias Island, cut off from the mainland by a deep, steep gully.

expect.title: Bodyboarding
expect.text: A popular bodyboarding beach; surfers often head next door to Constantine Bay.

expect.title: The rock pool
expect.text: At low tide a part-built rock pool fills with seawater and makes a handy natural pool for older children to swim in.

expect.title: Trethias Island
expect.text: The island off the headland, separated from the mainland by a steep gully.

goodToKnow.label: Danger on the left
goodToKnow.text: The left-hand side of the beach is dangerous: the tide comes in fast around the island and can cut people off. Keep an eye on it.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: The car park is often full at busy times, so arrive early.

week.text: A fun, sociable beach near Padstow for families and dog owners alike. Walk along to Constantine Bay next door for more space.

tips: Arrive early in summer: the car park fills quickly.
Watch the tide on the left-hand side of the beach.
